title: Golf Course Architect
author: sacker
rules:
There’s a canvas in those rolling hills… Where others see grid lines, you envision the unconstraint of wandering fairways. Where others see borders, you see an opportunity for opening it all up from the tees to the greens. Where others see control, you see inhibition. You want freedom. You want beautiful chaos. Today, that’s all yours. Today, you’re a golf course architect.

Solve this puzzle in SudokuPad.

Golf Course Design (Chaos Construction): Divide the grid into nine orthogonally connected regions (holes) of nine cells each. Each row, column, and region must contain the digits 1–9 exactly once.

Tee Boxes (Killer Cages): Each region begins at its tee box cell. The tee box cells are given as cages, where the number in each cage indicates the hole number (and the digit in that cage). The course is to be played from holes 1-9, in order.

Flag: Each flag cell is the final cell in its region; it is orthogonally adjacent to the subsequent tee box. The flag cell is also orthogonally adjacent to only one other cell in its region. (Also, the 9th flag is orthogonally adjacent to the 1st tee box.)

Hole Length: Each hole’s length is the minimum, orthogonal number of cells from the region’s tee box to its flag. This distance must not pass through other regions.

Par: Each tee box cell is orthogonally adjacent to only one other cell in its region. The digit in this “second” cell for each region represents a signpost indicating the hole’s par. Par for each hole is no less than two below the hole length and no greater than the hole length.

Bunkers (Dutch Whispers): Adjacent digits along an orange bunker line differ by at least 4. Digits along the same bunker must be within the same region.

Pond: The pond (blue dot) connects two digits with a ratio of 1:2 (one digit is double the other), and is located between a flag and the subsequent tee box.

Playing a Round: After the course is constructed, you give it a whirl and play nine holes! The digit in the flag cell represents your score for that hole. After the 9-hole round, you score 4 over par (in other words, the sum of the flag cells is 4 more than the sum of the par cells). Not bad for your first round, but maybe you can do even better on the back nine...
solutionCode: Your scorecard (digits in the flag cells from holes 1-9, in order)
